binders: n is an arbitrary natural number, possibly zero.
u is an arbitrary real number.
A and R are arbitrary functions Fin n -> Fin n -> Real, interpreted as square n-by-n real matrices indexed from 0 to n-1.
The symmetry and error hypotheses universally quantify over all i,j in Fin n, with the error hypothesis conditional on i.val <= j.val.
The conclusion existentially quantifies an n-by-n real matrix Delta A; this witness may depend on n, u, A, R, and the supplied hypotheses.
hypotheses: The real parameter u is nonnegative: 0 <= u.
A is symmetric: for every i,j in Fin n, A_{ij} = A_{ji}.
For every i,j in Fin n with i.val <= j.val, |sum over k in Fin n of R_{ki}R_{kj} - A_{ij}| <= (i.val+2)u times sum over k in Fin n of |R_{ki}||R_{kj}|.
conclusions: There exists an n-by-n real matrix Delta A such that, exactly and entrywise, sum over k in Fin n of R_{ki}R_{kj} = A_{ij} + Delta A_{ij} for every i,j.
For every i,j in Fin n, |Delta A_{ij}| <= (i.val+2)u times sum over k in Fin n of |R_{ki}||R_{kj}|.
For every i,j in Fin n, |Delta A_{ij}| <= (n+1)u times sum over k in Fin n of |R_{ki}||R_{kj}|.
mathematical_definitions: Write I_n = {0,1,...,n-1}; Fin n represents I_n, and i.val is the corresponding zero-based natural index.
The transpose is defined by (R^T)_{ij} = R_{ji}.
Let P = R^T R, so P_{ij} = sum_{k in I_n} R_{ki}R_{kj}.
Let W = |R|^T|R|, where absolute values are entrywise, so W_{ij} = sum_{k in I_n} |R_{ki}||R_{kj}|.
Matrix addition is pointwise, so P = A + Delta A means P_{ij} = A_{ij} + Delta A_{ij} for all i,j.
The natural quantities i.val+2 and n+1 are computed in the natural numbers and then embedded exactly into the real numbers.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every dimension n, every nonnegative real u, every symmetric real n-by-n matrix A, and every real n-by-n matrix R, suppose that each upper-triangular entry of R^T R differs from the corresponding entry of A by at most (i+2)u times the corresponding entry of |R|^T|R|, where i is the zero-based row index. Then there is a real matrix Delta A for which R^T R = A + Delta A exactly, and every entry Delta A_{ij} is bounded in absolute value both by (i+2)u(|R|^T|R|)_{ij} and by (n+1)u(|R|^T|R|)_{ij}.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The dimension n is unrestricted and may be zero. When n=0 there are no indices, all entrywise hypotheses and bounds are vacuous, and the matrix equality is an equality between functions on an empty domain.
Matrix indices are zero-based. Thus i+2 ranges from 2 through n+1 when n is positive.
The assumed residual bound is only for upper-triangular pairs i <= j; no lower-triangular residual bound is directly assumed.
The conclusion is purely entrywise and uses scalar absolute values. It states no matrix-norm bound.
No triangularity, nonsingularity, positivity, definiteness, or other structural property of R is assumed.
The only condition on u is nonnegativity; no strict positivity, smallness condition, or upper bound is encoded.
Delta A is not explicitly required to be symmetric, although the exact equation together with symmetry of A and of R^T R mathematically forces it to be symmetric.
The exact equation uniquely determines Delta A as R^T R - A, even though the declaration presents it existentially.
The second bound with coefficient n+1 is asserted in addition to the row-dependent bound; it is not a separate norm statement.
No floating-point operations, rounding function, algorithm, or computed matrix are represented explicitly. All displayed sums and arithmetic operations are exact real quantities.
